prompt: A meal-kit company wants to double revenue in three years. The candidate's framework: (1) Grow the existing customer base; (2) Increase order frequency and basket size; (3) Launch new products such as ready-to-eat meals; (4) Increase revenue per customer. What is the flaw in this framework?

options.text: Missing: marketing to win new subscribers
options.feedback: Winning new subscribers is how the customer base grows, which is bucket 1.

options.text: Bucket 3 doesn't belong: new products are separate from growth
options.feedback: Ready-to-eat meals could be a large source of new revenue, so new products belong in a growth framework.

options.text: It's a generic growth list: these levers would fit almost any company
options.feedback: The levers are specific to a meal-kit subscription: order frequency, basket size, ready-to-eat meals. The flaw is that bucket 4 repeats bucket 2.

options.text: Buckets 2 and 4 overlap: revenue per customer is frequency × basket
options.feedback: Right. Revenue per customer is order frequency × basket size, so bucket 4 repeats bucket 2. Use the slot for new channels, such as grocery stores or corporate meals.

explanation: Revenue per customer = order frequency × basket size, so buckets 2 and 4 repeat each other. Better: more customers, more revenue per customer, new products, new channels or geographies.

extras.corrected_framework: More customers; more revenue per customer (frequency, basket); new products; new channels or markets
